circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that loops around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds an FIA Grade 1 license. It serves as the venue for the Australian Grand Prix and various supporting motorsport events each year.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following renovation and reconfiguration as the A1-Ring, the venue resumed hosting the Grand Prix from 1997 through 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, spanning 6. 003 km and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix the following year.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. The FIA Grade 1-licensed venue accommodates various motorsports including GP2 Series and endurance racing, alongside hosting Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010, and features multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km motorsport facility is renowned for its balanced combination of high-speed straights and diverse corner designs, making it suitable for testing various racing capabilities. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand areas.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated near the town of Spa in Belgium's Wallonia region, this 7-kilometre circuit has been hosting Formula One racing since 1950 and has become the permanent home of the Belgian Grand Prix. The track has maintained continuous annual Grand Prix events since 1985, with only two interruptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361 km temporary street circuit hosts the Canadian Grand Prix, one of Formula One's marquee races. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport categories including sports car championships and North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit has served as the primary venue for China's Formula One grand prix, which ran from 2004 through 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track also accommodates other major motorsport events, including electric racing competitions that began in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue situated near Northamptonshire that became the birthplace of Formula One's World Championship when it hosted the inaugural championship race in 1950. Originally sharing the British Grand Prix with rival circuits between 1955 and 1986, Silverstone secured permanent status as Britain's Formula One home from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km racetrack located near Budapest, Hungary, hosting the annual Hungarian Grand Prix. Constructed in just eight months starting in late 1985, it became the venue for Formula One's first championship race held within the Eastern Bloc when it debuted in March 1986, commemorating pioneering Hungarian motorcycle racer János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit spans 5. 793 km and has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949, making it one of the most enduring venues on the Formula One calendar. Constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility, the track earned its nickname "Temple of Speed" for featuring long straights and fast-flowing corners that encourage high-velocity racing.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. Hosting major Formula One and Super Formula championships, the track features a seating capacity of 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street-based racing layout that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, adjacent to Las Vegas proper. The track follows portions of Las Vegas Boulevard, threading past iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a course that weaves among the city's premier hotels and entertainment destinations.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit located in Mexico City, named in tribute to brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom perished in racing accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, having previously held the race on a different configuration until 1992, with the event now officially designated as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that produces average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, it has hosted the Miami Grand Prix since the track's 2022 championship debut, with a modified configuration also adopted by Formula E beginning in the 2025-26 season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, winding around Monaco's harbor in the principality. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to the majority of its layout occupying that particular neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Situated in the Dutch coastal dunes 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km track hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining Formula One in 2021, though the partnership concluded in 2026. The venue, originally known as Circuit Park Zandvoort, has operated under various sponsorship names throughout its recent history.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motorsport venue situated near the city of Lusail, approximately north of Doha. Spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aviation accident in 1977. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an associated karting facility dedicated to fellow racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, situated along the Red Sea waterfront. Since 2021, it has been the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and it also hosts a major electric racing series event starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometre Spanish circuit features a balanced design with extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing various racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track hosts major motorsport events including NASCAR, MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas, and the FIA World Endurance Championship's Lone Star Le Mans race.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having claimed two world titles during his time with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 race victories across two decades. Beyond Formula One, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both a Formula One world championship and a World Endurance championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, where he has already secured eight Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British driver currently racing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team, representing one of the sport's major automotive manufacturers in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas brings extensive Formula One experience to Cadillac, having accumulated ten race victories throughout his thirteen-year career in the sport. Previously with Mercedes, he achieved back-to-back runner-up finishes in the 2019 and 2020 championship standings.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine, bringing his racing talent to the grid.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, serves as a reserve driver for Haas in Formula One while competing in the European Le Mans Series for Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category. He has participated in seven Grand Prix events between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One. He previously secured a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver competing in Formula One for Red Bull Racing, representing France in the championship.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who shares the record for most championship titles with seven wins, matching Michael Schumacher's achievement. He holds multiple Formula One records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver for Ferrari, finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver who previously competed in Formula One across two separate periods from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he competes as a factory driver for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT, while also undertaking part-time NASCAR Cup Series commitments with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver competing for McLaren who secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship with the team. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Earlier in his career, he secured a victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that has yielded six Grand Prix victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," Ricciardo has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Mercedes who has secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, having secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American racing driver who competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin. Known by his shortened surname in motorsport, Strulovitch has established himself as a competitor in the sport's top tier.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently holding reserve responsibilities with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing as a full-time competitor in Formula One between 2021 and 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently serving as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the championship as a full-time driver from 2022 to 2024 and holds the distinction of being the only Chinese driver to have participated in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, rebranded to showcase Renault's sports car marque while continuing as the manufacturer's works operation. Previously operating as Renault F1 Team under the broader automotive group, Alpine maintained this factory status until Renault's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has a long-standing presence in Formula One through multiple incarnations of its racing operations. The team currently competes under the banner of AMR GP Limited, operating as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari and stands as the sport's most enduring and triumphant competitor, participating continuously in the World Championship since its inaugural 1950 season. The team, famously nicknamed after their distinctive equine emblem, remains unparalleled in longevity and achievement within Formula One.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: TGR Haas F1 Team is an American-based Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR entrepreneur Gene Haas and launched competitively in 2016. The squad has been under the leadership of Ayao Komatsu since January 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who oversaw the team from its establishment through his departure earlier that year.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss motorsport engineering firm established in 1970, the organization initially competed in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. The team accumulated significant achievements across both disciplines, including a Le Mans victory in 1989, though it underwent numerous structural changes during its three-decade tenure in grand prix racing before ceasing operations in 2025. Audi acquired the operation and its infrastructure in 2024 to establish the technical foundation for its own Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the broader McLaren Group, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One as both a constructor and engine supplier since 1954, with the current team operating from Brackley under a German licence. The squad, now known as Mercedes-AMG Petronas, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff from 2022 onwards, and shares the "Silver Arrows" heritage associated with Mercedes racing efforts.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as a second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's expansion into a dual-team structure within the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team functions alongside Red Bull Racing as a sister outfit within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from its English base, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and became one of two championship teams within the Red Bull GmbH portfolio. The outfit experienced two decades of leadership under Christian Horner before his departure in 2025, with Laurent Mekies assuming the team principal role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team banner and operates from a substantial purpose-built facility.
